messages.content: The project code has been released. Go ahead with the St. Louis flights now: Wednesday evening out and Friday after the unpacking work. I need enough time to get back to the hotel for my bag before heading to the airport.

I’ll check current inventory for Wednesday, July 16 from Atlanta to St. Louis and Friday, July 18 back to Atlanta. For Friday, I’ll allow for the 2:00 p.m. finish, the trip from the museum to the Forest Park hotel, luggage retrieval, and airport security before comparing the departures.
Yes. The 7:10 Wednesday nonstop was the one we had identified, and the 6:20 Friday nonstop looked best.

The Wednesday flight is still available: nonstop, departing Atlanta at 7:10 p.m. and arriving in St. Louis at 7:50 p.m. local time. Economy is $214. The Friday inventory has changed. The 4:10 p.m. nonstop is $238, but it would leave only about 45 minutes at the airport after the estimated hotel stop and ride to the terminal, so I would not consider that workable. The 6:20 p.m. nonstop has no economy seats left; the only remaining seat is in first class at $1,048. There is also a 5:55 p.m. economy flight with one stop in Nashville, arriving in Atlanta at 10:38 p.m., for $286.
How much airport time would the 5:55 option give me if unpacking really ends at 2:00?

Using a conservative schedule, you would leave the museum around 2:15, reach the hotel near 2:35, collect your bag by 2:45, and arrive at the airport around 3:10. That gives you about two hours and forty-five minutes before departure. The Nashville connection is 58 minutes. The tradeoff is the connection and a later arrival in Atlanta, but the preflight margin is comfortable.
Is there any other nonstop later Friday in economy?

No. The 4:10 p.m. departure is the last Friday nonstop with economy inventory. The 6:20 p.m. flight remains available only in first class. Later economy itineraries all require one stop, and the 5:55 p.m. option is the earliest of them.
Then for this St. Louis trip, I’m willing to take the one-stop return. I don’t want to rush out of the museum or risk missing the 4:10, and I’m not charging a thousand-dollar seat to the project.

Understood. The itinerary would be the Wednesday 7:10 p.m. nonstop from Atlanta to St. Louis for $214, then the Friday 5:55 p.m. one-stop return through Nashville for $286, arriving in Atlanta at 10:38 p.m. The airfare is $500 before any optional extras. Shall I book both flights in economy using the traveler and project payment details on file?
Yes, book those flights. Use project code STL-LH-417 and the payment method already attached to my work profile.

The booking has been completed. Your outbound departs Atlanta on Wednesday, July 16 at 7:10 p.m. and arrives in St. Louis at 7:50 p.m. local time, nonstop. Your return departs St. Louis on Friday, July 18 at 5:55 p.m., connects in Nashville for 58 minutes, and arrives in Atlanta at 10:38 p.m. Both flights are in economy. The total charged to the work payment method under project code STL-LH-417 is $500.
Give me the confirmation number and make sure the return is clearly shown as the one-stop itinerary, not the old 6:20 plan.

Confirmation number ATL7QK covers both flights. The confirmed return is the Friday, July 18 one-stop itinerary: St. Louis departure at 5:55 p.m., 58-minute connection in Nashville, and Atlanta arrival at 10:38 p.m. The previously considered 6:20 p.m. nonstop is not booked. The outbound remains the Wednesday, July 16 nonstop departing Atlanta at 7:10 p.m. and arriving in St. Louis at 7:50 p.m. local time.
